description: Layer B golden fixture (DECK_PARITY_ARCHITECTURE.md §6.2): reserved-control-key geometry as a pure function of (key_rows, key_cols), degenerate-grid handling, session/view paging, and the control-key content table. Cannot differ legitimately between the soft deck (frontend/deck/deck.js) and the muxplex-deck hardware sidecar -- if a client's own implementation disagrees with a case here, that disagreement is a bug, not a deliberate per-device choice (the test for which is DECK_PARITY_ARCHITECTURE.md §5's 'would that be a bug?' question).
owner: muxplex (frontend/deck/deck.js) -- this repo authors the file today. The muxplex-deck sidecar should adopt this exact path/schema as its own `spec/deck-layout.fixtures.json` and assert the SAME cases from its Python test suite; whichever repo edits a case first bumps spec_version and the other repo re-syncs a byte-identical copy. See DECK_PARITY_ARCHITECTURE.md §6.2 for the full ownership rationale.

asserted_by.soft_deck: frontend/tests/test_deck.mjs (reservedControlKeys, sessionSlotIndices, pageCount, pageSlice, clampPage, controlKeyContent)
asserted_by.hardware_sidecar: muxplex-deck/tests/test_layout.py (layout.py's _reserved_control_keys and interaction.py's Pager) -- NOT YET WIRED to this file; out of scope for this change, tracked separately

cases.description: Stream Deck XL geometry (32 keys, 4 rows x 8 cols) -- also the soft deck's own N_MAX ceiling.
Stream Deck Original V2 geometry (15 keys, 3 rows x 5 cols).
3-column grid: the corners layout would put VIEW/PREV/NEXT too close together, so cols===3 && rows>=2 gets a dedicated bottom row instead (PREV, VIEW, NEXT left to right).
A single row: the corners formula collapses VIEW and PREV onto the same index (both 0) -- no controls fit, every key becomes a session tile.
A single column: the corners formula collapses PREV and NEXT onto the same index -- same degenerate handling as single-row.
Fewer than 4 keys total: no room for 3 reserved controls plus at least one session slot.

Stream Deck+ FULL layout (8 keys + 4 dials + touch strip) -- HARDWARE ONLY. The soft deck has no dials/touch-strip concept (DESIGN_SOFTDECK.md: a phone is always dial_count=0, is_touch=false) and its reservedControlKeys(rows, cols) takes no dial_count/is_touch input, so this case is structurally inapplicable to the JS harness -- it exists only for the sidecar's own test suite to assert against.
